title: What If You Dropped a Penny From the Empire State Building?

scenes.text: A penny falls from the Empire State Building. Why can't it hurt you?
After only about fifty feet, it stops speeding up. Air pushes back, and its top speed is roughly twenty-five miles an hour.
A penny is tiny, flat and light, about two and a half grams. It flutters and tumbles instead of diving like a bullet.
Take the air away and it would hit about two hundred and eight miles an hour. The air is what saves you.
Instead it lands like a flick on the forehead. The physicist Louis Bloomfield was hit by coins in his tests and walked away fine.
Dropping it from higher changes nothing. The speed limit comes from the penny's shape, not the height of the tower.

description:
What if you dropped a penny from the Empire State Building?
It hits a top speed of roughly 25 miles an hour after about 50 feet, then falls no faster. The feeling is a flick on the forehead, not a bullet.
